samples.summary: The "copies agree" half of the mirror test compares checks.mjs against a hand-typed copy inside the test, not against anything read out of the YAML — it cannot detect the drift it claims to pin
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:555-573 defines `const inline = (runs) => {...}` locally and then asserts `ciRunsToRerun(fixture)` deep-equals `inline(fixture)`. `inline` is a third copy living in the test file; it is not extracted, parsed, or evaluated from agent-rerun.yml / agent-loop.yml. So this loop is true regardless of what the workflows contain: editing either YAML block (or deleting the whole re-run step's logic) leaves these six fixtures passing. The failure message ("the inline mirror disagrees with ciRunsToRerun") therefore overstates what is verified — the only real coupling to the YAML is the regex assertions at :537-549, which pin text fragments (`red.length ? red : completed.slice(0, 1)`, `for (const run of`) without checking that the loop actually iterates the selected set. Impact is contained (a stuck agent loop, not user data), but the test is presented as drift protection it does not provide.

samples.summary: The YAML-pinning assertions run against a fixed byte window (`at - 200 .. at + 900`) anchored on the first `workflow_id: 'ci.yml'` occurrence, so they can pass or check the wrong code after unrelated edits
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:533-535: `const at = yml.indexOf("workflow_id: 'ci.yml'"); const block = yml.slice(at - 200, at + 900);`. Two fragilities that weaken the guard rather than the suite's greenness: (a) the negative assertion `assert.ok(!/per_page: 1,/.test(block))` at :537 is only meaningful while the offending text would fall inside that 1100-byte window — a regression that reintroduces a single-run fetch a few lines further down (e.g. a second listWorkflowRuns call, as agent-iterate-ci.yml already has at :172) is invisible; (b) if either workflow gains an earlier `workflow_id: 'ci.yml'` step, `indexOf` anchors on that unrelated block and the assertions no longer describe the re-run step at all. A structural extraction (locate the `reRunWorkflow` call and slice around it) would be robust.

searchedFor: grep ciRunsToRerun across repo (only checks.mjs, checks.test.mjs, a docs task note)
samples.summary: `ciRunsToRerun` has no production caller — the unit test at :493 covers a specification replica, while the code that actually runs (the two inline YAML blocks) has no behavioral test
samples.evidence: grep shows `ciRunsToRerun` referenced only in checks.mjs (its definition), checks.test.mjs, and a docs note; both real call sites (.github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:202-207, agent-loop.yml:167-172) reimplement the rule inline and never import it. So the well-written test at checks.test.mjs:493-521 exercises a function nothing invokes at runtime, and the shipped behavior (paginate all runs, re-run every red one, fall back to one green run, skip in-flight) is only asserted via source-text regexes. Nothing verifies, for example, that the workflow re-runs each selected run or that a 422 on the second run does not falsely leave `reran = true`. Given the repo's own precedent for inline mirrors this may be the accepted ceiling, but the coverage is narrower than the test's framing suggests.

searchedFor: compare checks.mjs:121-125 (`r?.status`) with the inline copies (`r.status`)
samples.summary: The agreement fixtures never include a null/undefined element or a run with a missing `status`, the one input class where `ciRunsToRerun` (`r?.status`) and both inline copies (`r.status`) genuinely differ
samples.evidence: checks.mjs:122 uses optional chaining (`r?.status === "completed"`), while agent-rerun.yml:202 and agent-loop.yml:167 use `r.status === 'completed'`, which throws on a null element. The six fixtures at checks.test.mjs:560-567 are all well-formed objects, so the deliberate hardening in the exported copy is untested and the divergence from the mirrors is unrecorded. Low impact (the API is unlikely to return null entries), but it is the exact case the agreement loop was written to catch.
